page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.24xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio designed for memory-intensive computations without dedicated GPU acceleration.

The instance delivers a baseline network throughput of 32 Gbps, supporting significant data transfer volume across cloud infrastructure. Because local storage is absent, all persistent and scratch disk operations require external network-attached block storage volumes. Public IPv4 connectivity must be configured independently, as no complimentary addresses are assigned by default.

From an architectural standpoint, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers operational cost efficiency when running workloads that bottleneck on memory footprint rather than raw processing frequency. The lack of built-in NVMe storage requires careful consideration of remote storage bandwidth limits, making this profile best suited for enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caches, high-capacity analytical processing, and large-scale ETL pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture and hosted on KVM hypervisors. Driven by 96 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at 2.7 GHz, it provides 768.0 GB of total RAM, delivering an 8.0 GB per-core memory ratio. Network connectivity operates at a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps. The instance contains zero local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring all persistent file systems and databases to utilize remote block storage solutions. It also features no integrated graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given the extensive memory allocation and multi-core AMD density, the ecs.r8a.24xlarge is optimized for memory-bound enterprise operations including in-memory databases, big data batch processing, distributed caching layers, and high-volume data analytics engines.
